settings.label: Files to analyze
settings.description: Files to analyze. Environment variables are expanded and glob patterns are supported.

settings.label: Rule options per file
settings.description: A list of single key maps from a file name or glob pattern to a configuration with a rule key, applied to the files it matches.

settings.label: Index files
settings.description: Files which are read, but not analyzed, so rules such as port_028 also see the instantiations in them.

settings.label: Local rule directories
settings.description: Directories with local rules to load.

settings.label: Lint mode
settings.description: Also run the lint checks, labelled with the checks of the rule set. The same as --lint.

settings.label: Lint only
settings.description: Run only the lint checks and the rules of the rule set. The same as --lint_only.

settings.label: Rule set
settings.description: Rule set for lint mode: a built in name such as do254, the path of a YAML file, or none for all lint rules without labels.

settings.label: Waivers
settings.description: Findings accepted with a justification: each waiver names a rule (an identifier, alias or pattern) and a justification, and optionally a file pattern, a line or lines, a message pattern and a reviewer. Waived findings do not fail the run and are listed in the reports.

settings.label: Design top entity
settings.description: The top entity of the design analyzed with --design.

settings.label: Design top architecture
settings.description: The architecture of the top entity. GHDL chooses the last analyzed one when it is not set.

settings.label: VHDL standard
settings.description: The VHDL standard GHDL analyzes the design with.

settings.label: Design libraries
settings.description: The libraries of the design in analysis order. Each has a name and files, a list of files and glob patterns, or files_from, a file listing them.

settings.label: Top library
settings.description: The library of the top entity. The last library when it is not set.

settings.label: Top generics
settings.description: Values of the generics of the top entity, by name.

settings.label: Design work directory
settings.description: Keeps the files of GHDL and Yosys in this directory. A temporary directory is used and removed when it is not set.

settings.label: Clock domain crossing constraints
settings.description: Names of clock sources (clocks), groups of synchronous clocks (clock_groups), the clock domains of input ports (inputs) and crossings waived with a justification (waivers).

settings.label: Vendor libraries
settings.description: Vendor component declarations to analyze before the design, read from the vendor installation: xilinx, microchip, intel or lattice, or a library with its files.

settings.label: Black box declarations
settings.description: Maps black box types, such as vendor primitives, to the clock domain role of each port, or to an archetype. Every black box must be declared.

settings.label: Black box libraries
settings.description: YAML files with black_boxes and black_box_instances, shared between designs. The design section takes precedence.

settings.label: Black box instance declarations
settings.description: Maps instance paths or patterns to declarations that take precedence over the declaration of their type.

settings.label: GHDL options
settings.description: Extra options for GHDL, such as -fsynopsys.

settings.label: Line separator
settings.description: The line separator for fixed files. The platform default is used when it is not set.

settings.label: Custom severities
settings.description: Maps names of custom severities to a map with a type key, error or warning. The names can then be used in the severity option of rules.

settings.label: Opening pragmas
settings.description: Regular expressions for comments which open a pragma region, such as -- synthesis translate_off.

settings.label: Closing pragmas
settings.description: Regular expressions for comments which close a pragma region, such as -- synthesis translate_on.

settings.label: Single pragmas
settings.description: Regular expressions for pragma comments which stand on their own.

settings.label: Align comments with the end of a declarative part
settings.description: Indent of a comment at the end of a declarative part: true uses the current indent level, false the next indent level.

settings.label: Align comments with the end of a statement part
settings.description: Indent of a comment at the end of a statement part: true uses the current indent level, false the next indent level.

settings.label: Indent of tokens
settings.description: The indent of each token (token) and of the lines after it (after), by token group and token name. A value is an indent level, current to keep the current level, or a string such as +1 or -1 relative to the current level.

rule_scopes.description: Options of one rule. Takes precedence over group and global options.
Options for every rule in a rule group, see rule_groups. Takes precedence over global options.
Options for every rule that has an option of that name.

action:move_token_rules.label: Action
action:move_token_rules.description: new_line moves the token to the next line; move_left moves it left next to the previous non-whitespace token. Any value other than new_line moves the token left.

action:optional_items.label: Action
action:optional_items.description: add inserts the optional VHDL item if it is missing; remove deletes it if present.

action:pragma_100.label: Action
action:pragma_100.description: add requires one space after the -- of a pragma; remove requires none. A pragma is only changed if the result still matches a pragma pattern.

action:record_type_definition_001.label: Action
action:record_type_definition_001.description: new_line moves the record keyword to its own line; same_line (default) and move_left keep it on the line of the type declaration. Any value other than new_line moves it left.

after_generic_map_aspect.label: New line after generic map
after_generic_map_aspect.description: Whether the port map keyword starts a new line after a generic map aspect: add_new_line requires a line break, remove_new_line removes it.

after_instantiated_unit.label: New line after instantiated unit
after_instantiated_unit.description: Whether the port map keyword starts a new line after the instantiated unit: add_new_line requires a line break, remove_new_line removes it.

aggregate_parens_ends_group.label: Aggregate parenthesis ends group
aggregate_parens_ends_group.description: yes ends the alignment group at an aggregate parenthesis, no continues through it, per_level aligns each aggregate on its own and continues the enclosing group after it. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_else_keywords.label: Align else keywords
align_else_keywords.description: yes column-aligns the else keywords of a conditional assignment; no leaves them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left.label: Align left
align_left.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator; on_new_line_after_assign aligns left only when a line break follows the assignment. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:concurrent_401.label: Align left
align_left:concurrent_401.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:constant_012.label: Align left
align_left:constant_012.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:sequential_402.label: Align left
align_left:sequential_402.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:signal_402.label: Align left
align_left:signal_402.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:variable_402.label: Align left
align_left:variable_402.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_left:variable_assignment_401.label: Align left
align_left:variable_assignment_401.description: yes indents continuation lines from the left; no aligns them to the assignment operator. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_paren.label: Align parenthesis
align_paren.description: yes aligns continuation lines to the unbalanced open parenthesis; no adds one indent per unbalanced open parenthesis. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

align_to.label: Align to
align_to.description: keyword aligns to the keyword named by the rule; current_indent aligns to the current indent level.

align_when_keywords.label: Align when keywords
align_when_keywords.description: yes column-aligns the when keywords of a conditional assignment; no leaves them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

alignment.label: Alignment
alignment.description: report aligns continuation lines after the first keyword (report or when); left indents them by a fixed amount from the statement indent.

allow_indenting.label: Allow indenting
allow_indenting.description: yes also detects indented block comments; no only detects block comments starting in column 0. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

allow_library_clause.label: Allow library clause
allow_library_clause.description: yes allows a library clause directly above another library clause without a blank line; no applies the style normally. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

allow_single_line.label: Allow single line
allow_single_line.description: yes allows a conditional signal assignment with a single else to stay on one line; no requires a line break after every else. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

allowed_numbers.label: Allowed numbers
allowed_numbers.description: The numbers that may be written in statements, such as 0 and 1.

array_constraint.label: Array constraint
array_constraint.description: all_in_one_line puts all dimensions of an array constraint on one line; one_line_per_dimension puts each dimension on its own line; ignore skips the check.

assign_on_single_line.label: Assign on single line
assign_on_single_line.description: yes forces each element association (choice => value) onto a single line; ignore allows it to span lines. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

association_element.label: Association element
association_element.description: Line break before each association element of a procedure call. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

association_list_comma.label: Association list comma
association_list_comma.description: Line break before each comma of the association list. remove_new_line keeps commas at line ends, ignore skips the check; add_new_line (accepted, not documented) moves commas to the start of the next line.

attributes.label: Attributes
attributes.description: Attribute names, such as fsm_safe_state, of which a state signal must have one so synthesis keeps the recovery logic. Empty means not checked.

blank_line_ends_group.label: Blank line ends group
blank_line_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at a blank line; no aligns across blank lines. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

blank_lines_allowed.label: Blank lines allowed
blank_lines_allowed.description: Maximum number of consecutive blank lines allowed; extra blank lines are removed.

case.label: Case
case.description: Case to enforce. camelCase and PascalCase allow at most two uppercase letters in a row, the relaxed forms any number; regex requires a full match of the regex option.

case_control_statements_ends_group.label: Case control statements end group
case_control_statements_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at case, when and end case; no aligns across them; break_on_case_or_end_case only breaks at case and end case. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

case_exceptions.label: Case exceptions
case_exceptions.description: Words that are accepted when written exactly as listed, regardless of the case option.

clock.label: Clock style
clock.description: event requires clk'event and clk = '1' style clock checks; edge requires rising_edge(clk) and falling_edge(clk).

clock_words.label: Clock words
clock_words.description: Word patterns (file-name style * and [0-9]) that mark a port as a clock; port names are split into words at underscores.

close_paren_new_line.label: Close parenthesis new line
close_paren_new_line.description: yes adds a line break before each close parenthesis of the array, no removes it, ignore skips the check. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

comment_left.label: Comment left
comment_left.description: String that must follow the -- of every line inside a block comment, e.g. |. None (empty) disables the check.

comment_line_ends_group.label: Comment line ends group
comment_line_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at a comment line; no aligns across comment lines. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

compact_alignment.label: Compact alignment
compact_alignment.description: yes aligns to the left-most possible column (one space after the longest line part); no aligns to the right-most existing position. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

consecutive:number_of_signals_in_signal_.label: Names per declaration
consecutive:number_of_signals_in_signal_.description: Maximum number of signals allowed in a single signal declaration.

consecutive:number_of_variables_in_varia.label: Names per declaration
consecutive:number_of_variables_in_varia.description: Maximum number of variables allowed in a single variable declaration.

differential_suffixes.label: Differential suffixes
differential_suffixes.description: Pairs [positive, negative] of suffixes of differential ports; both ports of a pair are sorted together by their shared name, positive first.

direction.label: Range direction
direction.description: The direction the ranges of vectors run in.

direction_order.label: Direction order
direction_order.description: Order of the port modes for the direction sort key. A port without a mode counts as in.

disable.label: Disable
disable.description: Turns the rule off when true. Rules that are disabled by default must be set to false to run.

exceptions:comment_100.label: Exceptions
exceptions:comment_100.description: Comment starts (exactly three characters, beginning with --) after which no space is required, e.g. --! or ---.

exceptions:multiline_constraint_rules.label: Exceptions
exceptions:multiline_constraint_rules.description: Named exceptions to enable. keep_record_constraint_with_single_element_on_one_line keeps a record constraint with a single element on one line.

exceptions:prefix_and_suffix_rules.label: Exceptions
exceptions:prefix_and_suffix_rules.description: Regular expressions matched from the start of the name, ignoring case; matching names are not checked for the prefix or suffix.

exempt_unique.label: Exempt unique case
exempt_unique.description: yes lets a unique or unique0 case statement go without a default item; no requires one in every case statement. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

first_open_paren.label: First open parenthesis
first_open_paren.description: Line break before the opening parenthesis of the parameter list. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

first_paren_new_line.label: First parenthesis new line
first_paren_new_line.description: yes adds a line break before the first parenthesis of the array, no removes it, ignore skips the check. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

fixable.label: Fixable
fixable.description: When false, the rule still reports violations but --fix does not change the code.

follow_resets.label: Follow synchronous resets
follow_resets.description: Also report signals that meet through a synchronous reset, an input that loads a constant into two or more registers.

footer_alignment.label: Footer alignment
footer_alignment.description: Horizontal position of footer_string within the footer line.

footer_left.label: Footer left
footer_left.description: String placed directly after the -- of the footer line. None means nothing.

footer_left_repeat.label: Footer left repeat
footer_left_repeat.description: Character repeated between footer_left and footer_string (or to the end of the line when there is no footer_string).

footer_right_repeat.label: Footer right repeat
footer_right_repeat.description: Character repeated after footer_string up to max_footer_column. Required when footer_string is set.

footer_string.label: Footer string
footer_string.description: Text placed in the footer line, positioned by footer_alignment. None means no text.

generate_statement_ends_group.label: Generate statement ends group
generate_statement_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at generate statement keywords; no aligns across them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

header_alignment.label: Header alignment
header_alignment.description: Horizontal position of header_string within the header line.

header_left.label: Header left
header_left.description: String placed directly after the -- of the header line. None means nothing.

header_left_repeat.label: Header left repeat
header_left_repeat.description: Character repeated between header_left and header_string (or to the end of the line when there is no header_string).

header_right_repeat.label: Header right repeat
header_right_repeat.description: Character repeated after header_string up to max_header_column. Required when header_string is set.

header_string.label: Header string
header_string.description: Text placed in the header line, positioned by header_alignment. None means no text.

if_control_statements_ends_group.label: If control statements end group
if_control_statements_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at if, elsif, else and end if; no aligns across them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

ignore_single_line.label: Ignore single line
ignore_single_line.description: yes skips statements that fit on a single line; no checks them as well. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

ignore_single_line_aggregates.label: Ignore single line aggregates
ignore_single_line_aggregates.description: yes skips aggregates that fit on a single line when aligning; no includes them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

ignore_spaces_before_numbers.label: Ignore spaces before numbers
ignore_spaces_before_numbers.description: When true, spaces between an open parenthesis and a following number are allowed.

include_lines_without_comments.label: Include lines without comments
include_lines_without_comments.description: yes also counts code lines without a trailing comment when choosing the comment column, so comments line up right of all code in the group; no ignores those lines. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

include_type_is_keyword.label: Include type is keyword
include_type_is_keyword.description: yes aligns the is keyword of type declarations with the colons; no ignores it. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

indent_size.label: Indent size
indent_size.description: Number of spaces per indent level used by the rule.

indent_style.label: Indent style
indent_style.description: spaces indents with spaces only; smart_tabs indents with tabs and aligns with spaces.

interface_element.label: Interface element
interface_element.description: Line break before each interface element (parameter) of the subprogram specification. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

interface_list_semicolon.label: Interface list semicolon
interface_list_semicolon.description: Line break before each semicolon of the parameter list. remove_new_line keeps semicolons at line ends, ignore skips the check; add_new_line (accepted, not documented) moves them to the start of the next line.

keywords.label: Keywords
keywords.description: Keywords (case sensitive, whole words) that are reported when found in a comment, such as TODO or FIXME.

last_close_paren.label: Last close parenthesis
last_close_paren.description: Line break before the closing parenthesis of the parameter list. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

last_paren_new_line.label: Last parenthesis new line
last_paren_new_line.description: yes adds a line break before the last parenthesis of the array, no removes it, ignore skips the check. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

length:length_002.label: Length
length:length_002.description: Maximum number of lines in a file.

length:length_003.label: Length
length:length_003.description: Maximum number of lines in a process.

length:length_004.label: Length
length:length_004.description: Second, usually larger, line length limit in characters with its own severity.

localparam_pattern.label: Localparam pattern
localparam_pattern.description: Regular expression a localparam name must match in full; the default is UpperCamelCase, as in Verible.

loop_control_statements_ends_group.label: Loop control statements end group
loop_control_statements_ends_group.description: yes starts a new alignment group at loop statement keywords (including for and while loops); no aligns across them. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

magnitude.label: Delay magnitude
magnitude.description: Number of time units used in the after clause added to signal assignments, e.g. 1 for after 1 ns.

max_footer_column.label: Max footer column
max_footer_column.description: Total length of the footer line, including its indent.

max_header_column.label: Max header column
max_header_column.description: Total length of the header line, including its indent.

maximum.label: Longest name
maximum.description: The most characters in a name other than that of a module or instance.

maximum_depth.label: Maximum logic depth
maximum_depth.description: The most logic levels a combinational path may have, counting operators such as adders, comparisons and multiplexers.

method.label: Instantiation method
method.description: component requires component instantiations; entity requires direct entity instantiations.

min_height.label: Minimum height
min_height.description: Minimum number of consecutive comment lines before they are treated as a block comment.

minimum.label: Shortest name
minimum.description: The fewest characters in a name other than that of a module or instance.

minimum_percent.label: Minimum comment share
minimum_percent.description: The share of the lines of a file, in percent, that must have a comment.

module_maximum.label: Longest module name
module_maximum.description: The most characters in the name of a module or instance.

module_minimum.label: Shortest module name
module_minimum.description: The fewest characters in the name of a module or instance.

move_generics.label: Move generics
move_generics.description: never only reports the expected order; when_safe also moves the generics of an entity if no file of the run instantiates it with positional generic association.

move_ports.label: Move ports
move_ports.description: never only reports the expected order; when_safe also moves the ports of an entity if no file of the run instantiates it with positional association.

names:architecture_025.label: Names
names:architecture_025.description: Allowed architecture names as regular expressions (full match, ignoring case); other names are reported.

names:library_012.label: Names
names:library_012.description: Forbidden library names as regular expressions (full match, ignoring case).

names:use_clause_001.label: Names
names:use_clause_001.description: Forbidden package names as regular expressions (full match, ignoring case).

nesting_limit.label: Nesting limit
nesting_limit.description: The deepest nesting of if, case and loop statements allowed.

new_line_after_assign.label: New line after assignment
new_line_after_assign.description: yes adds a line break after the assignment operator, no removes it, ignore skips the check. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

new_line_after_comma.label: New line after comma
new_line_after_comma.description: yes adds a line break after each comma, no removes it, ignore skips the check, ignore_positional adds it unless the elements are positional. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

number_of_spaces.label: Number of spaces
number_of_spaces.description: Spaces required: an integer for an exact count, or a string >N, >=N or N+ for a minimum, <N or <=N for a maximum.

open_paren_new_line.label: Open parenthesis new line
open_paren_new_line.description: yes adds a line break after each open parenthesis of the array, no removes it, ignore skips the check. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

order:port_028.label: Order
order:port_028.description: Sort keys for the ports, most important first: clock_reset (clocks, then resets, then others), direction (see direction_order) and name.

order:port_map_012.label: Order
order:port_map_012.description: declaration follows the port order of the entity or component declaration; name sorts the associations by formal name.

parameter_pattern.label: Parameter pattern
parameter_pattern.description: Regular expression a parameter name must match in full; the default is UpperCamelCase or ALL_CAPS, as in Verible.

parenthesis.label: Parenthesis
parenthesis.description: insert requires the if condition to be enclosed in parentheses; remove removes the enclosing parentheses.

pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.description: Regular expression a requirement tag comment must match, such as the default for -- REQ HWR-123 written with a colon after REQ.

pattern:sv_comment_001.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_comment_001.description: Regular expression searched for in comments; a comment it matches is reported.

pattern:sv_generate_002.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_generate_002.description: Regular expression the label of a generate block must match in full; the default (g_|gen_).* follows Verible.

pattern:sv_naming_002.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_002.description: Regular expression the name of an enum type must match in full.

pattern:sv_naming_003.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_003.description: Regular expression the name of a struct or union type must match in full.

pattern:sv_naming_004.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_004.description: Regular expression the name of an interface must match in full.

pattern:sv_naming_005.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_005.description: Regular expression the name of a macro must match in full; macros named uvm_ may be lower case.

pattern:sv_naming_006.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_006.description: Regular expression the name of a constraint must match in full.

pattern:sv_naming_008.label: Pattern
pattern:sv_naming_008.description: Regular expression the name of a signal or port must match in full.

patterns.label: Patterns
patterns.description: Comment starts (beginning with --) after which a space is inserted, e.g. --! becomes --! text.

phase.label: Phase
phase.description: Phase (1 to 7) in which the rule runs; rules run in increasing phase order. Changing it is rarely needed and can break the ordering between rules.

policy.label: Alignment policy
policy.description: infer aligns the column, keeps it flush left or leaves it, by how the author spaced it, as Verible's formatter does; align always aligns; flush_left always uses the fewest spaces.

prefix_exceptions.label: Prefix exceptions
prefix_exceptions.description: Prefixes (found ignoring case) that must be written as listed; the case option is applied to the rest of the word.

prefixes.label: Prefixes
prefixes.description: Allowed prefixes, compared ignoring case. The fix uses the first one.

prefixes:sv_naming_011.label: Prefixes
prefixes:sv_naming_011.description: Prefixes no name may start with, compared ignoring case; by default those of power and ground nets.

qualifier_words.label: Qualifier words
qualifier_words.description: Word patterns that stop a port from counting as a clock or reset, e.g. en in clk_en.

record_constraint_close_paren.label: Record constraint close parenthesis
record_constraint_close_paren.description: Line break before the closing parenthesis of a record constraint. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

record_constraint_comma.label: Record constraint comma
record_constraint_comma.description: Line break before each comma of a record constraint. remove_new_line keeps commas at line ends, ignore skips the check; add_new_line (accepted, not documented) moves them to the next line.

record_constraint_element.label: Record constraint element
record_constraint_element.description: Line break before each element of a record constraint. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

record_constraint_open_paren.label: Record constraint open parenthesis
record_constraint_open_paren.description: Line break before the opening parenthesis of a record constraint. add_new_line forces a line break, remove_new_line removes it, ignore skips the check.

regex.label: Regex
regex.description: Regular expression the word must fully match when case is set to regex. Empty by default.

regex_exceptions.label: Regex exceptions
regex_exceptions.description: Regular expressions matched from the start of the word, ignoring case; matching words are not checked.

remove_prefixes.label: Remove prefixes
remove_prefixes.description: Prefixes removed from a local declaration before the fix adds the first allowed prefix.

remove_suffixes.label: Remove suffixes
remove_suffixes.description: Suffixes removed from a local declaration before the fix adds the first allowed suffix.

required_fields.label: Required header fields
required_fields.description: Fields the header comment of each file must have, each written as its name followed by a colon.

reset_words.label: Reset words
reset_words.description: Word patterns (file-name style * and [0-9]) that mark a port as a reset; port names are split into words at underscores.

section_pattern.label: Section pattern
section_pattern.description: Regular expression that one of the comment lines directly above each group must match. The default accepts any comment.

separate_generic_port_alignment.label: Separate generic and port alignment
separate_generic_port_alignment.description: yes aligns generic and port clauses (or maps) separately; no aligns them as one group. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

severity.label: Severity
severity.description: Name of the severity reported for violations: Error or Warning, or a custom name defined under the top-level severity key with type error or warning.

sort_within_sections.label: Sort within sections
sort_within_sections.description: yes sorts each group separated by a blank line or comment line on its own; no sorts the whole list. Booleans true/false are also accepted.

spaces.label: Spaces
spaces.description: The least number of spaces between code and a comment at the end of its line.

spaces_after.label: Spaces after mode
spaces_after.description: Number of spaces required after the port mode.

spaces_before.label: Spaces before mode
spaces_before.description: Number of spaces required before the port mode.

standard.label: VHDL standard
standard.description: VHDL standard whose reserved words may not be used as names; all uses the words of every standard. Years must be quoted strings.

strip_prefixes.label: Prefixes to ignore
strip_prefixes.description: Prefixes ignored when the name of a signal is compared with the name of the port it is connected to.

strip_suffixes.label: Suffixes to ignore
strip_suffixes.description: Suffixes ignored when the name of a signal is compared with the name of the port it is connected to.

style:architecture_016.label: Style
style:architecture_016.description: require_blank_line requires a blank line; no_blank_line removes blank lines.

This rule aligns the names of the port declarations of a module, interface or program header in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the opening parentheses of the named port connections of an instance in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the opening parentheses of the named parameter assignments of an instance in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the names of consecutive variable and net declarations in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the assignment operators of consecutive continuous assignments and assignment statements in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the = of consecutive parameter and localparam declarations, and of the parameters of a header in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the statements of case items written on the line of their item in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.

This rule aligns the names of the members of a struct or union in a column, as Verible's formatter does. By default it infers whether the author meant them aligned or flush left; policy set to align or flush_left forces one.
This rule checks that combinational logic uses always_comb rather than always @ or always @().
This rule checks that always_comb blocks use blocking assignments (=), not nonblocking ones (<=).

This rule checks that sequential logic, in always_ff blocks and in always blocks clocked on an edge, uses nonblocking assignments (<=). Blocking assignments in the header of a for loop are allowed; with waive_for_locals set to yes, so are blocking assignments to variables declared in the block.
This rule checks that an always block does not mix blocking (=) and nonblocking (<=) assignments. Assignments in the header of a for loop are not counted.
This rule checks that an always block has a single event control, at its start, as the STARC guide asks (2.2.2.3). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that an always block holds at most one if or case statement at its top level, as the STARC guide asks (2.6.2.1). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for blank lines at the end of a file, which Verible's formatter removes.
This rule checks that a case statement has a default item, unless it is unique or unique0 and exempt_unique is yes, the default.
This rule checks that the default item of a case statement is its last item.
This rule checks for case statements whose selector is a constant, such as case (1'b1), as the STARC guide asks (2.8.5.2). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.

This rule checks for synthesis directives and scripts in comments, such as synopsys full_case, parallel_case or dc_script_begin, as the STARC guide asks (2.8.1.5, 2.8.5.1, 3.1.2.7). pattern is the regular expression searched for in comments. It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that parameters and localparams are declared with a type, such as int or logic [7:0], as Verible's explicit-parameter-storage-type rule does.
This rule checks that packed dimensions are written from the most to the least significant bit, such as [7:0], as Verible's packed-dimensions-range-ordering rule does.
This rule checks that unpacked dimensions are written as [0:N-1] or [N], as Verible's unpacked-dimensions-range-ordering rule does.
This rule checks a file holding modules is named after one of them, as Verible's module-filename rule does: counter.sv holds module counter.
This rule checks a file holding a package is named after it, as Verible's package-filename rule does: fifo_pkg.sv holds package fifo_pkg.
This rule checks a file holds at most one module, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.1.1). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that include directives name files by relative paths, as the STARC guide asks (3.2.2.4). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that functions outside classes are declared automatic or static, as Verible's explicit-function-lifetime rule does; the fix adds automatic.
This rule checks that tasks outside classes are declared automatic or static, as Verible's explicit-task-lifetime rule does; the fix adds automatic.
This rule checks that the arguments of functions and tasks are declared with a type, as Verible's explicit-function-task-parameter-type rule does.

This rule checks for nonblocking assignments (<=) in functions, as the STARC guide asks (2.1.2.2). Methods of classes, such as the drivers of a testbench writing to a virtual interface, are not checked.
This rule checks for tasks in design code, as the STARC guide asks (2.1.2.4): use functions. It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that the begin-end blocks of generate loops, ifs and cases are labelled.
This rule checks that the labels of generate blocks match pattern, a regular expression, by default (g_|gen_).*, as Verible's generate-label-prefix rule does.
This rule checks for begin-end blocks directly in a generate region, a Verilog-2001 form.
This rule checks for generate regions: the generate and endgenerate keywords are not needed.
This rule checks for genvar declarations outside of a for loop; declare the genvar in the loop instead.
This rule checks the indent of SystemVerilog and Verilog code.
This rule checks that the label after end matches the label of its begin. An end label without a begin label is removed.
This rule checks for widths that do not match, such as an assignment that truncates a value, as slang reports them (WidthTruncate, WidthExpand, PortWidthTruncate and PortWidthExpand).
This rule checks for latches: variables that combinational logic does not assign on every path.
This rule checks for variables driven by more than one process or continuous assignment.

This rule checks for nets declared implicitly by their use, which hides typing mistakes; the default_nettype none directive makes them errors. A file that uses modules, packages or macros of other files is not checked, as a name defined there would look like an implicit net.

This rule checks for declarations that are never used: ports, variables, nets, parameters and imports, and variables assigned but never read. A file that uses modules, packages or macros of other files is not checked, as a signal read there would look unused.
This rule checks for case items that duplicate or overlap others, which can never be matched.
This rule checks for comparisons and conversions between signed and unsigned values.

This rule checks that the sensitivity list of a combinational always block names every signal and port of the file that the block reads. A missing signal makes simulation differ from synthesis; always_comb or always @* avoids the list altogether.
This rule reports the other warnings slang finds when it elaborates the file, such as an index out of range or arithmetic between operands of different types, with slang's name of the warning.
This rule checks for variables, nets and output ports that nothing drives. A file that uses modules, packages or macros of other files is not checked, as a signal driven there would look undriven.

This rule reports the warnings of Verilator, when it is installed, for checks slang does not make: blocking assignments in clocked processes (BLKSEQ), non-blocking assignments in combinational ones (COMBDLY), and others. The verilator_warnings option lists the warnings reported, by Verilator's names; by default those whose checks slang does not make, but for MULTIDRIVEN and CASEINCOMPLETE, which sv_lint_012 and sv_lint_013 report.

This rule reports signals assigned in always blocks of different clocks (Verilator's MULTIDRIVEN), which synthesis cannot build as one register. Verilator lints the SystemVerilog files of a run when it is installed, see sv_lint_011.

This rule reports case statements that do not cover every value of their selector and have no default branch (Verilator's CASEINCOMPLETE). Verilator lints the SystemVerilog files of a run when it is installed, see sv_lint_011.
This rule checks that a sized binary literal has a digit for each bit, as Verible's undersized-binary-literal rule does; the fix adds leading zeros. Zero, as in 4'b0, is allowed.
This rule checks that the value of a sized literal fits its width, as Verible's truncated-numeric-literal rule does.
This rule checks that parameter values are written with an explicit base, such as 'd8, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.4.8). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that a literal whose value needs more than 32 bits has an explicit width, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.4.9). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for comparisons with x or z, which are never true in synthesis, as the STARC guide asks (2.10.1.4). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for begin-end blocks directly in a module, outside of any generate construct.
This rule checks for defparam statements; set parameters in the instantiation instead.

This rule checks that parameter names match parameter_pattern and localparam names match localparam_pattern, regular expressions, by default UpperCamelCase or ALL_CAPS for parameters and UpperCamelCase for localparams, as Verible's parameter-name-style rule does.
This rule checks that the names of enum types match pattern, a regular expression, by default [a-z_0-9]+(_t|_e), as Verible's enum-name-style rule does.
This rule checks that the names of struct and union types match pattern, a regular expression, by default [a-z_0-9]+_t, as Verible's struct-union-name-style rule does.
This rule checks that interface names match pattern, a regular expression, by default [a-z_0-9]+_if, as Verible's interface-name-style rule does.
This rule checks that macro names match pattern, a regular expression, by default [A-Z_0-9]+, as Verible's macro-name-style rule does; macros whose names start with uvm_ or UVM_ may be lower case.
This rule checks that constraint names match pattern, a regular expression, by default ([a-z0-9]+_)+c, as Verible's constraint-name-style rule does.
This rule checks that no parameter name starts with disable; name it after what it enables, as Verible's positive-meaning-parameter-name rule does.

This rule checks that the names of signals and ports match pattern, a regular expression, by default lower_snake_case [a-z_0-9]+, as Verible's signal-name-style rule does. It is disabled by default, as in Verible.

This rule checks that names use only letters, digits and underscores and start with a letter, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.1.2): no escaped identifiers and no leading underscore. It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.

This rule checks that no name is a VHDL keyword, in any case, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.1.3), so the design can be translated or mixed with VHDL. SystemVerilog keywords cannot be names. It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that no name starts with VDD, VSS, VCC, GND or VREF, in any case, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.1.4). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks that no two names of a file differ only in case, as the STARC guide asks (1.1.1.5). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.

This rule checks the length of names, as the STARC guide asks: modules and instances module_minimum to module_maximum characters, 2 to 32 by default (1.1.2.1); other names minimum to maximum, 2 to 40 by default (1.1.3.3). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.

This rule checks that the statement of an if, else, for, foreach, while, repeat, forever, always or initial is a begin-end block, as Verible's explicit-begin rule does. An else if needs no block of its own.
This rule checks for consecutive null statements, such as ;;.
This rule checks for more than one statement or declaration on a line, as the STARC guide asks (3.1.4.4, at most one assignment per line). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for initial blocks in design code, which synthesis ignores, as the STARC guide asks (2.3.4.1, 2.3.4.2). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for fork-join blocks in design code, as the STARC guide asks (2.7.4.3). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule checks for empty branches of if and case statements, such as a case item with only a semicolon, as the STARC guide asks (2.7.2.3). It is disabled by default; the starc rule set enables it.
This rule reports code slang cannot parse. The rules on constructs, such as always blocks and labels, skip a file with syntax errors, as its syntax tree has constructs missing or misplaced.
This rule checks that enum types are declared with typedef, not anonymously in a declaration, as Verible's typedef-enums rule does.
This rule checks that struct and union types are declared with typedef, not anonymously in a declaration, as Verible's typedef-structs-unions rule does.
This rule checks for no space before a comma, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for at least one space after a comma, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space before a semicolon, except one after the colon of an empty case item (default: ;), as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for at least one space after a semicolon followed by more code on the line, as in a for loop, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for one space between if, for, foreach, while, repeat, wait or case and its opening parenthesis, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space between @ and its parenthesis or *, and one space between an always keyword and @, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space after # in parameter lists and delays, as Verible's formatter does.

This rule checks for at least one space around binary and assignment operators and the ? and : of a conditional expression, except in the brackets of a select or a dimension, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space between a unary operator and its operand, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space between ++ or -- and its operand, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space between the name of a function, task or system task and its argument list, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space between a name and the bracket of a select, such as data[0]; the packed dimensions of a type, as in data_t [1:0], keep their space, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for one space on each side of the colon of a block label, such as begin : name and end : name, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for no space before the colon of a case item and at least one after it, as Verible's formatter does.
This rule checks for at least spaces spaces, 2 by default, between code and a comment at the end of its line, as Verible's formatter does.
